The Assistant Commissioner of Vijayanagar Sub- division, Bengaluru , has submitted the charge sheet against the accused No.1 to 3 for the offence punishable U/s.498-A, 304-B r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 3 and 4 of Dowry Prevention Act in Crime No.374/2017 of their PS. SC No.1730/2018 2.

sentences.text:
The gist of the prosecution case is that, the marriage of accused No.1 with the deceased Smt.
Roopa was solemnized on 05.06.2017 in presence of elders of the family at Basaveshwara Temple situated in Yukthapur, Surapura Taluk, Yadagiri district.
At the time of the marriage the accused persons stated to have received 100 grams of gold jewelry on demand as dowry from the parents of deceased.
Thereafter they harassed the deceased Smt. Roopa for petty reasons and the accused persons often finding fault in every work she did including the food prepared by her.
The accused No.1 is running grocery shop in Basanaveshwara nagar, Bengaluru city as such the couple shifted to Bengaluru and started to reside in said area.

On 28.12.2017 again all the accused persons demanded additional dowry of Rs. 15 lakhs for business of accused No.1 and also 40 grams gold, and to meet their illegal demands the accused have allegedly harassed the deceased.

Therefore on 28.12.2017 between 12.00 p.m. to 6.00 p.m. the deceased being fed up with the harassment of her husband and in laws has committed suicide by hanging self with ceiling fan in the bed room and thereby it is alleged that accused persons have harassed her and instigated her to end the life and thereby the accused persons have committed the offences PUS 498A and 304B R/w Section 34 of IPC along with sections 3 and 4 of DP Act.

2 3.
Since the charge sheet was submitted against the accused No.1 to 3 before the jurisdictional learned V Addl. CMM Court Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate after taking cognizance of said offences has complied with provisions of section 207 of Cr,P.C.

Since the offence punishable U/sec.
SC No.1730/2018 304(B) r/w 34 of IPC is triable by Sessions court as such the learned V ACMM Bengaluru has committed the case and it was registered in as Sessions Case register.
In response to the summons issued by this court the accused persons appeared through their advocate and they were formally released on bail on 05.03.2019.
4. The charge was framed against the accused No.1 to 3 on 24.02.2020 for the offences punishable U/s. U/s.498-A, 304-B r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 3 and 4 of DP Act as alleged against them.
The accused No.1 to 3 pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

5. As such the following points arises for consideration:
1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1 to 3 after receiving dowry at the time of marriage have while residing in house No.1066, 5th main, 3rd stage, 3rd block, Sanegurammanahalli, Basaveshwara nagara,
Bengaluru made demand for additional dowry and for said purpose they have subjected the deceased Smt. Roopa to mental and physical cruelty which drives the deceased to commit suicide and thereby committed the offence PUS 498-A of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the deceased Smt.. Roopa being fed up with mental and physical torture of accused No.1 to 3 while residing in her matrimonial home situated at the address given above on 28.12.2017 between 12-00 noon to 6-00 pm in the evening hanged self with a SC No.1730/2018 ceiling fan in her bed room and committed suicide and thereby the accused No.1 to 3 have committed the offence PUS 304B R/w Section 34 of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1 to 3 at the time of the marriage on demand received 100 grams gold as dowry from parents of deceased and after the marriage they have demanded for additional dowry from her parents and thereby committed the offences PUS 3 and 4 of DP Act?
4. What order?
6. In order to prove the guilt of accused the prosecution in all got examined 21 witnesses as PW.1 to PW.21 and got marked as many as 28 documents at Ex.P-1 to P-28.
Further the prosecution has also relied upon one material object as per MO-1 and Ex.C-1.

Thereafter the statement of accused was recorded on 29-01-2024 as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C. The accused has denied all the incriminating evidence against them after taking several adjournments they filed a memo stating that, they have no defense evidence.

3 7.

Thereafter I have heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record my finding on the above point is as under:
Point No.1: In Negative.
Point No.2: In Negative.
Point No.3: In Negative.
Point No.4:

As per final order for the following:-
SC No.1730/2018 REASONS 8 .Point No.1 to 4:-As these points are interconnected to each other, I have taken together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts and evidence.
PW-1 and PW- 10 father and mother respectively of the deceased have deposed to the effect that, they had three children CW-2 is their son and deceased was their 3 rd daughter.

The marriage of their deceased daughter Smt.
Roopa was solemnized on 05- 06-2017 with accused No.1 and they lived happy married life while residing in a house situated in Basaweshwara Nagar Bengaluru.
But on 28-12-2017 in the afternoon their daughter committed suicide in her matrimonial home hanging self and said fact was informed by her husband to 2 nd daughter of PW-1 and 10.
Immediately they rushed to Bengaluru from Vijaypura to the place of offence where the police were already present and they transported the dead body to the hospital for post mortem.

Next day morning they visited the police station since the police instructed PW-1 to give a complaint regarding death of their daughter as such when he was in grief of death of his daughter he put his signature on a document which was prepared by the police himself.
Accordingly, PW-1 identified his signature on complaint Ex.P-1 as per Ex.P-1(a).

But PW-1 has clarified in the very chief examination that, he does not know as to the contents of Ex.P-1 and he also did not lodge any complaint against the accused persons of dowry harassment which led to the suicidal death of his daughter.
The witness identified the wedding invitation card and photograph taken at the time of marriage at Ex.P-2 and 3 respectively.
PW-2 son of PW-1 SC No.1730/2018 and 10 has deposed in corroboration to the evidence of his parents and he also completely turned hostile to the prosecution case.

9. The learned Public Prosecutor has exhaustively cross examined them by bringing their attention to the contents of Ex.P-1 and their statements recorded before the Investigating Officer (In Short referred to as IO).
But they have denied all the suggestions and leading questions put to them by the learned Prosecutor.

10. PW-3 relative of PW-1 has deposed that, he only knew about deceased Roopa as she is daughter of CW-1 who died in the year 2017 but he does not know how and for what reason she died and clarified that, he did not give any statement before the Tahsildar regarding cause of death of Roopa.
The learned PP has cross examined this witness by bringing his attention to the contents of his statement at Ex.P- 9 but he also denied all the suggestions put to him by the learned PP.

PW-4 and PW-5 have deposed to the effect that, the police have prepared a mahazar as per Ex.P-10 at the Basaveshwaranagara Ps vs A-1 Prabhugowda on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80587673/
4 scene of crime in their presence.
They have also taken photograph of deceased as per Ex.P-5 and identified their signatures on mahazar at Ex.P-10(a) and (b) respectively.

They are cross examined by the defense lawyer wherein the witnesses have admitted that, they do not know the boundaries of place of offence or place of mahazar and they also do not know as to cause of death of Smt. Roopa.

However another mahazar witness PW-8 has identified her signature on said document at Ex.P-(c)
but she has deposed that, the police SC No.1730/2018 did not prepare Ex.P-10 in her presence nor she is aware about its contents.

In this manner she has turned hostile though the learned PP has cross examined about the contents of said document but she denied all the leading questions put to her.
11. PW-6 and 7 signatories to the inquest mahazar Ex.P-7 have identified their signatures as per Ex.P-7(a) and (b) respectively but they have denied about preparation of any such mahazar in the mortuary of Victoria hospital Bengaluru by the learned Tahsildar.

The learned PP cross examined them by bringing their attention to the contents of Ex.P-7 but they have denied all the suggestions put to them and in this manner they too turned hostile to the prosecution case. PW-9 is witness to Ex.P-11 a seizure mahazar prepared by the IO during investigation but this witness only identified his signature on said document at Ex.P-11(a) and denied of seizure of clothes wear by the deceased at the time of her death and further clarified that, no such mahazar was prepared by the IO in his presence.
The learned PP has cross examined him by drawing his attention to the contents of seizure mahazar but he denied all the suggestions made to him by the learned Public Prosecutor.

12. PW-11 and 12 sister and junior uncle of deceased Smt. Roopa have deposed to the effect that, the marriage of said Roopa with accused No.1 was solemnized on 05-06-2017 in Yadgir district and the couple lived happily in matrimonial home at Bengaluru.
The police took the dead body of said Roopa from the scene of crime for post mortem by the doctor.
But they have deposed nothing against any of the accused be it with respect to dowry demand and receipt by the accused at the time of marriage or subsequent to the marriage.
They have also clarified that, they did not give any statement before the IO against the accused persons regarding dowry harassment which led Roopa to commit suicide in her matrimonial home.

The learned PP has cross examined them at length by bringing their attention to the contents of their statements at Ex.P-13 and 14 but they have denied all the suggestions made to them regarding the alleged incident.
In this manner these two important witnesses also turned hostile to the prosecution case.

13. PW-13, PW-14, PW-15 and PW-16 all are relatives of deceased and her father PW-1 but they have deposed to the effect that, deceased Roopa is daughter of PW-1 but they do not know how and for what reason she died in her matrimonial home.
They have deposed that, Smt. Roopa died in the year 2017 but they do not know whether she committed suicide due to dowry harassment given by the accused persons.
They have further clarified that, the Tahsildar has not recorded their statements as per Ex.P-15, P-16, P-17 and Ex.P-18 respectively.
PW-17 a neighbor of deceased Roopa and he has deposed that, he know the accused and deceased but he does not know why Roopa died and he also does not know the reason behind her death.
In the year 2017 the police had visited the house of accused in Basawaeshwar nagar at that time the police had told him about death of Roopa.

But he Basaveshwaranagara Ps vs A-1 Prabhugowda on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80587673/
5 did not give a statement before the police regarding cause of her death and alleged harassment given to SC No.1730/2018 her by the accused as per Ex.P-19.
The learned PP has cross examined them at length but they have not admitted to any of the leading question or suggestions made to them by the learned Prosecutor.
In this manner they have turned hostile to the prosecution case.
14. PW-18 is a doctor and an medical expert from FSL working in Victoria hospital Bengaluru.
He has deposed to the effect that, on 29-12-2017 as per the request of Tahsildar Bengaluru North he has done post mortem on dead body of deceased Smt. Roopa between 7-45 pm to 8-30 pm.
The witness has described the injuries found on her body, he deposed regarding issuance of PM report in respect of deceased Smt. Roopa as per Ex.P-20 and identified signature at Ex.P-20(a).
He further deposed that, he has handed over all the material objects found on body of deceased such as Saree by which she had hanged self with ceiling fan.

The witness has identified the requisition, model seal and the opinion given by him regarding cause of death at Ex.P-21, P- 22 and P-23 and identified signatures at Ex.P-21(a), P-22(a) and P-23(a) respectively, the saree is marked at MO-1.
The doctor has opined that, the death of Smt. Roopa was due to asphyxia as a result of hanging and deposed with regard to sending of blood and viscera for chemical analysis.
The witness has also deposed that, as per the request of the IO he give opinion that, the MO-1 saree can bear the weight of deceased.

15. PW-19 a alternate nodal officer from Info-Com Limited has deposed to the effect that, as per the instructions SC No.1730/2018 of Bengaluru police he has collected the cell phone call details in respect of Simcard number 7975777089 from 05-06-2017 till 29-12-2017.

Accordingly he has handed over all the call details to the IO as per Ex.P-25 and identified the requisition filed by the IO and the certificate regarding digital evidence as per Ex.P-24 and P-26 respectively.
PW-20 Tahsildar has deposed regarding preparation of inquest mahazar in presence of CW-3 and 4 and recording of statements of CW-2 and 5.
The witness has identified the inquest mahazar at Ex,-7 and signature at Ex.P-7 and thereafter he handed over the dead body to the hospital for conducting post mortem.
16. PW-21 has deposed that, on 28-12-2017 he was the SHO of Basaweshwarnagar PS.
In the midnight CW-2 came to the police station with a written report regarding death of her sister.
Thereafter he visited the place of offence with PSI Honnappa and CW-2.
He deposed regarding spot inspection and preparation of spot mahazar in presence of witnesses.
He also deposed regarding transportation of dead body to Victoria hospital for post mortem and other formalities.
He identified the report given by CW-2 at Ex.P-6 and signature at Ex.P-6(b).

The witness identified the daily diary at Ex.P-27 and signature at Ex.P-27(a) and requisition filed before the superior rank officer at Ex,P-28 signature at Ex.P-28(a), the spot mahazar at Ex,P-5 and signature at Ex.P5(d).
17.
Among 28 documents Ex.P-8, P-9 and Ex.P-12 to P-19 are all statements of witnesses who have turned hostile to the prosecution case.

The most important documents are Ex.P-1 the first information wherein it is SC No.1730/2018 alleged that, the accused persons at the time of marriage had received gold jewelry and other articles as dowry from parents of deceased Smt. Roopa.

After the marriage on 05-06-2017 the deceased while living with her husband and in laws the accused No.1 to 3 was subjected to mental and physical torture by the accused persons to bring additional dowry of Rs.14 lakhs for development of groceries of accused No.1 and other movables.

Since their demands were not met with as such the accused have harassed her and tortured and because of Basaveshwaranagara Ps vs A-1 Prabhugowda on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80587673/
6 unbearable torture on 28-12-2017 between 12 pm to 6-30 pm she has committed suicide at her matrimonial home by hanging self with a saree in her bed room.

Further it is relevant to note that,
in the left the deceased has written a death note stating that, the accused persons are responsible for her death.
18. As mentioned above the parents, brother and sister and all the relatives of the deceased have not supported the prosecution case and they completely turned hostile to the case.

Even the learned Public Prosecutor cross examined them by bringing their attention to the contents of Ex.P-1, their statements and the contents of spot and seizure mahazar including the statements recorded by the Tahsildar at the time of preparation of inquest Mahazar Ex.P-7 but they have denied all the suggestions made to them and disown about their statements recorded by the IO and Tahsildar SC No.1730/2018 both regarding the dowry harassment which led to the suicidal death of Smt. Roopa and the alleged role of the accused persons so as to attract the penal provisions of section 498A and 304B of IPC and section 3 and 4 of DP Act.
19.
The official witnesses, the doctor has deposed regarding the post mortem conducted by him on dead body of deceased Smt. Roopa.
The Tahsildar has deposed regarding preparation of inquest mahazar in Victoria hospital.
The nodal officer has deposed regarding collection of call details in respect of cell number given above.
But the parents, brother and sister of deceased did not complained of any cruelty or harassment to the deceased by the accused persons before her death.

Under such circumstances and in the absence of corroborative evidence from the material witnesses on the basis of evidence of official witnesses the case of prosecution cannot be accepted as proof of guilt of accused persons for the offences PUS 498A and 304B of IPC along with section 3 and 4 of DP Act.
20. The evidence of IO regarding registration of case, preparation of mahazar, recording of statements of witnesses etc is all about the post facto incident (death of Smt. Roopa).
The evidence of official witness would have been relevant had there been any support from the evidence of parents and relatives of the deceased.
But for the reasons best known to them all the material SC No.1730/2018 witnesses of prosecution case have turned hostile and not deposed anything against the accused persons.

21. Though the prosecution got marked several documents but the contents of important documents such as first information inquest mahazar and the phone call details are not proved in accordance with law.

Of course the dying declaration on left hand of the deceased Roopa blaming her husband for her unfortunate death is a very strong evidence but before relying on such evidence the prosecution has to prove the necessary ingredients of section 498A of IPC because the cause for her death was dowry harassment.
But her parents, siblings and all her relatives have deposed nothing about the dowry harassment to the deceased by the accused persons at any point of time.

Ex.C-1 two photographs showing the left hand of the deceased in her left palm the deceased said to have written a note stating that, her husband and his relatives are the reason for her unfortunate death.

But this evidence particularly evidence by itself is not sufficient to hold that, soon before her death Smt.
Roopa the wife of accused No.1 was subjected to harassment as per sections 498A and 304B of IPC.

Though PW-1 has identified the death note as per Ex.C-1 and said that, the left hand appearing in Basaveshwaranagara Ps vs A-1 Prabhugowda on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80587673/
7 photograph is of his deceased daughter but he flatly denied the suggestion that, his daughter committed suicide because of harassment given to her by the SC No.1730/2018 accused persons.

It is most relevant to note that, in order to accept the dying declaration or death note as appearing in Ex.C-1 the prosecution has to first prove that, the accused persons had subjected the deceased to mental and physical harassment soon before her death.

The death note as per the case of prosecution was written on 28-12-2017 but the accused have disputed the same and argued that, the writings appearing on left hand as per Ex.C-1 were not written by the deceased.

In this connection the prosecution has not only to prove the writings as per Ex.C-1 of deceased Smt. Roopa it has also to prove that, she committed suicide since she was subjected to harassment soon before her death.

Since the prosecution has failed to prove the necessary ingredients of sections 498A and 304B of IPC and section 3 and 4 of DP Act.
22.

After meaningful reading evidence of PW-1 to PW-17 it is evident that, there is no evidence to prove the allegations against the accused persons that, at the time of marriage between the accused No.1 and deceased there was any demand for dowry or receipt of it by the accused.

Further there is no iota of evidence to show that, the accused persons had ever made demand for additional dowry much less the dowry demand for Rs.14 lakhs for business and for that end they harassed her to meet their alleged illegal demands.

When the necessary ingredients of section 498A of IPC and sections 3 and 4 of DP Act are SC No.1730/2018 not established then a presumption as per section 113 of Indian Evidence Act cannot be raised so as to hold that, the prosecution has proved the guilt of accused persons for the offence PUS 304B of IPC.
23.

For the reasons mentioned above now it is crystal clear that, the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of accused No.1 to 3 for the offences PUS 498A and 304B R/w Section 34 of IPC and section 3 and 4 of DP Act beyond reasonable doubt.

Accordingly I answer the above point No.1 to 3 in Negative.
24
.POINT
No.4:-In view of answer of court on point No.1 to 3

, this court pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 to 3 are hereby acquitted from the charges leveled against them for the offense punishable U/s 498A, 304-B r/w 34 of IPC along with Sec. 3 and 4 of DP Act.
The bail bonds and surety bonds of the accused No.1 to 3 stand canceled.
MO1 being worthless is ordered to be destroyed after appeal period is over.

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the deceased Smt.. Roopa being fed up with mental and physical torture of accused No.1 to 3 while residing in her matrimonial home situated at the address given above on 28.12.2017 between 12-00 noon to 6-00 pm in the evening hanged self with a SC No.1730/2018 ceiling fan in her bed room and committed suicide and thereby the accused No.1 to 3 have committed the offence PUS 304B R/w Section 34 of IPC?
3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1 to 3 at the time of the marriage on demand received 100 grams gold as dowry from parents of deceased and after the marriage they have demanded for additional dowry from her parents and thereby committed the offences PUS 3 and 4 of DP Act?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Under such circumstances and in the absence of corroborative evidence from the material witnesses on the basis of evidence of official witnesses the case of prosecution cannot be accepted as proof of guilt of accused persons for the offences PUS 498A and 304B of IPC along with section 3 and 4 of DP Act.
20. The evidence of IO regarding registration of case, preparation of mahazar, recording of statements of witnesses etc is all about the post facto incident (death of Smt. Roopa).
The evidence of official witness would have been relevant had there been any support from the evidence of parents and relatives of the deceased.
But for the reasons best known to them all the material SC No.1730/2018 witnesses of prosecution case have turned hostile and not deposed anything against the accused persons.
21. Though the prosecution got marked several documents but the contents of important documents such as first information inquest mahazar and the phone call details are not proved in accordance with law.
Of course the dying declaration on left hand of the deceased Roopa blaming her husband for her unfortunate death is a very strong evidence but before relying on such evidence the prosecution has to prove the necessary ingredients of section 498A of IPC because the cause for her death was dowry harassment.
But her parents, siblings and all her relatives have deposed nothing about the dowry harassment to the deceased by the accused persons at any point of time.
But this evidence particularly evidence by itself is not sufficient to hold that, soon before her death Smt.
Roopa the wife of accused No.1 was subjected to harassment as per sections 498A and 304B of IPC.
In this connection the prosecution has not only to prove the writings as per Ex.C-1 of deceased Smt. Roopa it has also to prove that, she committed suicide since she was subjected to harassment soon before her death.
Since the prosecution has failed to prove the necessary ingredients of sections 498A and 304B of IPC and section 3 and 4 of DP Act.
22.
After meaningful reading evidence of PW-1 to PW-17 it is evident that, there is no evidence to prove the allegations against the accused persons that, at the time of marriage between the accused No.1 and deceased there was any demand for dowry or receipt of it by the accused.
Further there is no iota of evidence to show that, the accused persons had ever made demand for additional dowry much less the dowry demand for Rs.14 lakhs for business and for that end they harassed her to meet their alleged illegal demands.
When the necessary ingredients of section 498A of IPC and sections 3 and 4 of DP Act are SC No.1730/2018 not established then a presumption as per section 113 of Indian Evidence Act cannot be raised so as to hold that, the prosecution has proved the guilt of accused persons for the offence PUS 304B of IPC.
23.
For the reasons mentioned above now it is crystal clear that, the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of accused No.1 to 3 for the offences PUS 498A and 304B R/w Section 34 of IPC and section 3 and 4 of DP Act beyond reasonable doubt.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly I answer the above point No.1 to 3 in Negative.
24
.POINT
No.4:-In view of answer of court on point No.1 to 3
, this court pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 to 3 are hereby acquitted from the charges leveled against them for the offense punishable U/s 498A, 304-B r/w 34 of IPC along with Sec. 3 and 4 of DP Act.
The bail bonds and surety bonds of the accused No.1 to 3 stand canceled.
MO1 being worthless is ordered to be destroyed after appeal period is over.
